teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Begin with a discussion on what mixtures are and their characteristics. Ask students to provide examples from daily life (e.g., salad, air).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Present different separation techniques, filtration, evaporation, distillation, and when each method is best used.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Experiments on separation of different mixtures using different methods are correctly performed

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students will work in groups to classify a list of materials into homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Groups will present their classifications, and the class will discuss any discrepancies.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Experiments on separation of different mixtures using different methods are correctly performed

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: In groups, students will choose a separation method to present (e.g., filtration, evaporation) and outline how it works using examples.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Each group shares their findings. As a class, create a flowchart summarizing separation methods.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Experiments on separation of different mixtures using different methods are correctly performed
